en: I thought I would give you a little reading update.
zh: 我想给你们简单更新一下我最近的阅读情况。

en: because I've been reading Doppelganger by Naomi Klein, which came highly recommended to me.
zh: 因为我最近一直在读 Naomi Klein 的《Doppelganger》，这本书是别人强烈推荐给我的。

en: I'm really enjoying it.
zh: 我读得还挺享受的。

en: I also feel like I should have been taking notes when I started reading it
zh: 我也觉得自己一开始读的时候就应该做笔记。

en: because she covers so many different topics.
zh: 因为她在书里涉及的话题实在太多了。

en: ranging from COVID-19 and misinformation surrounding the pandemic.
zh: 从 COVID-19 到疫情期间围绕它出现的错误信息，都有讲到。

en: But for those of you that don't know.
zh: 不过对于不了解的人来说。

en: the book is essentially centered around the fact that.
zh: 这本书的核心其实是围绕这样一件事展开的。

en: Naomi Klein is frequently mistaken for Naomi Wolf online, not really in person as far as I know.
zh: Naomi Klein 经常在网上被误认成 Naomi Wolf，不过据我所知，现实生活中倒不太会这样。

en: But yeah, their names are quite similar.
zh: 不过是的，她们的名字确实很像。

en: They also, I think their husbands have incredibly similar names, which is quite eerie.
zh: 而且我觉得她们丈夫的名字也非常相似，这点还挺诡异的。

en: And then they do look kind of similar.
zh: 然后她们长得也确实有点像。

en: They both write sort of big idea books.
zh: 她们也都写那种偏大思想、大议题的书。

en: but Naomi Wolf became kind of a right wing, not even kind of like a right wing conspiracy theorist.
zh: 但 Naomi Wolf 变成了某种右翼人物，甚至不能说某种，就是一个右翼阴谋论者。

en: during the pandemic or maybe a little before that.
zh: 是在疫情期间，或者也可能稍微早一点。

en: But then she kind of rose to popularity during the pandemic.
zh: 不过后来她确实是在疫情期间变得更受关注了。

en: So that's what it is about.
zh: 所以这本书大概讲的就是这些。

en: I'm enjoying it, but it is giving me nightmares.
zh: 我读得挺喜欢的，但它也让我做噩梦。

en: And there's just so many topics that are discussed and they're kind of,
zh: 而且书里讨论的话题实在太多了，它们有点……

en: I feel like there's like a lot of sort of jumping around in the book,
zh: 我感觉这本书里有很多来回跳转的内容。

en: which I don't think is a bad thing, but yeah, it's a lot.
zh: 我倒不觉得这是坏事，但确实信息量很大。

en: And I can't believe I'm only a hundred pages in.
zh: 而且我不敢相信自己才读了一百页。

en: and there's still so much more.
zh: 后面居然还有那么多内容。

en: My introduction to Naomi Klein was actually.
zh: 我第一次接触 Naomi Klein，其实是。

en: when I worked at a Mexican restaurant, sometimes it would be really slow in the evening.
zh: 以前我在一家墨西哥餐厅工作的时候，晚上有时候真的很清闲。

en: And I had this coworker who would bring in the book, The Shock Doctrine by Naomi Klein.
zh: 我有一个同事会带 Naomi Klein 的《The Shock Doctrine》来。

en: And if it was really dead in the restaurant.
zh: 如果餐厅真的特别没客人。

en: all the staff would go and sit in the kitchen and he would just read us excerpts from The Shock Doctrine,
zh: 所有员工就会去厨房坐着，然后他会给我们读《The Shock Doctrine》里的摘录。

en: which is kind of a bizarre book to read as a group.
zh: 这本书拿来一群人一起读，其实还挺奇怪的。

en: That's kind of funny.
zh: 这事还挺好笑的。

en: But because this is nonfiction and it's like a lot of information.
zh: 不过因为这本书是非虚构作品，而且信息量真的很大。

en: and I feel like I have to be really on while I'm reading it,
zh: 我感觉自己读的时候必须特别集中注意力。

en: I do want to start some fiction.
zh: 所以我确实想开始读点小说。

en: I have a handful of books that I picked up at the bookstall that I went to on the weekend.
zh: 我手头有几本周末去书摊时买回来的书。

en: And I'm trying to decide if I want to read The Handmaid's Tale,
zh: 我现在在纠结要不要读《The Handmaid’s Tale》。

en: which shockingly I haven't read.
zh: 很震惊的是，我居然还没读过它。

en: I've never read anything by Margaret Atwood.
zh: 我从来没读过 Margaret Atwood 的任何作品。

en: which as a Canadian feels kind of crazy.
zh: 作为一个加拿大人，这感觉还挺离谱的。

en: I've always wanted to read Fear Flying.
zh: 我一直都想读《Fear Flying》。

en: And then there's some Daphne du Maurier's.
zh: 然后这里还有几本 Daphne du Maurier 的书。

en: I've already read Rebecca.
zh: 我已经读过《Rebecca》了。

en: I actually don't know why it's in this pile.
zh: 其实我也不知道它为什么会在这一堆里。

en: These two and then, oh, there's actually another one.
zh: 这两本，然后，哦，其实还有另一本。

en: It's called The Parasites.
zh: 它叫《The Parasites》。

en: I'm sort of leaning towards The Handmaid's Tale.
zh: 我现在有点倾向于读《The Handmaid’s Tale》。

en: because I also want to watch the show.
zh: 因为我也想看那部剧。

en: So maybe I should start The Handmaid's Tale first.
zh: 所以也许我应该先开始读《The Handmaid’s Tale》。

en: I have a general idea of what it's about.
zh: 我大概知道它讲的是什么。

en: So that could be interesting.
zh: 所以应该会挺有意思的。
